description: Papers concerning geometric or variational properties of knots, such as knot energies, curvature, regularity, or geometric optimization. Exclude papers whose primary focus is a discrete or combinatorial knot model rather than geometric analysis.

Papers in which curves of finite total curvature, or closely related geometric consequences of finite total curvature, are a substantive topic. Exclude papers where curvature appears only incidentally or refers to a substantially different notion.

Papers concerning symmetric critical points or symmetric critical configurations in geometric knot theory and knot-energy problems. Exclude general critical-point theory unrelated to knots or geometric knot energies.

Papers developing or applying regularity theory in the context of geometric knot theory, knot energies, or related variational problems. Exclude papers where regularity theory is unrelated to these geometric or knot-theoretic settings.

Papers about gradient flows arising from geometric variational problems. Exclude gradient-flow papers from unrelated areas such as quantum field theory, machine learning, statistical mechanics, or information geometry.

Papers where variational methods are a substantive tool in geometric analysis, including the study of geometric energies, critical points, minimizers, compactness, or variational properties of geometric objects. Exclude papers where variational methods are used primarily in non-geometric settings.

Papers studying the Palais-Smale condition, Palais-Smale sequences, or closely related compactness properties for functionals arising in geometric or geometric-variational problems. Exclude abstract Palais-Smale theory without a substantive geometric application and applications in unrelated physical or analytic settings.

Papers studying functionals defined using curvature or curvature-related geometric quantities, including their minimizers, critical points, regularity, compactness, or variational properties. Exclude papers where curvature is only incidental or where the main object is not a geometric functional.

query: Topological methods in calculus of variations
description: Papers using topological methods to study variational problems, including techniques such as critical point theory, minimax methods, category, degree theory, index methods, or topological arguments for existence and multiplicity of critical points. Exclude papers involving topology only incidentally or calculus of variations without a substantive topological component.

query: existence of minimizers in geometric variational problems
description: Papers establishing or studying existence of minimizers for geometric variational problems, including arguments based on compactness, coercivity, lower semicontinuity, direct methods, or related variational techniques. Exclude existence results for general differential equations or optimization problems that are not substantively geometric and variational.

query: concentration compactness in geometric variational problems
description: Papers using concentration-compactness principles or closely related compactness methods in geometric variational problems, including analysis of loss of compactness, bubbling, or concentration phenomena. Exclude concentration-compactness results in settings without a substantive geometric or variational component.

Papers applying Morse theory, Morse index methods, critical groups, or related topological techniques to variational problems and the study of critical points. Exclude purely finite-dimensional Morse theory or topological results without a substantive variational application.

Papers studying harmonic maps through variational principles, energy minimization, critical points of harmonic-map energies, or regularity and existence questions arising from these energies. Exclude papers where harmonic maps or minimization are only incidental.

Papers studying minimal surfaces or related minimal submanifolds using variational methods, including area minimization, critical points, compactness, regularity, or existence questions. Exclude papers on minimal surfaces without a substantive variational component.

Papers studying isoperimetric inequalities or isoperimetric minimization problems on Riemannian or related geometric manifolds, including existence, regularity, stability, or geometric properties of minimizers. Exclude purely Euclidean inequalities or unrelated optimization problems.

Papers where Sobolev inequalities, Sobolev-type estimates, or related functional inequalities play a substantive role in geometric analysis, including geometric PDE, variational problems, or analysis on manifolds. Exclude papers using Sobolev spaces only as routine background without a substantive inequality or geometric application.

Papers studying variational problems with free boundaries, including existence, regularity, minimization, singularities, or geometric properties of the free boundary. Exclude fixed-boundary variational problems and free-boundary problems without a substantive variational formulation.

Papers studying formation, structure, classification, or analysis of singularities in geometric evolution equations such as mean curvature flow, Ricci flow, or related geometric flows. Exclude singularities arising in unrelated dynamical systems or PDE without a substantive geometric-flow setting.

Papers applying Gamma-convergence or closely related variational convergence methods to geometric energies or geometric variational problems, including discrete-to-continuum limits, approximation, or convergence of minimizers. Exclude Gamma-convergence in non-geometric settings.

query: variational eigenvalue problems on geometric domains
description: Papers studying eigenvalue problems through variational principles in geometric settings, including manifolds, geometric domains, or shape-dependent spectral problems. Exclude purely algebraic spectral problems or eigenvalue calculations without a substantive variational and geometric component.
